thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — cluster-us-west-2: node(s) reporting ephemeral storage pressure > 92% on /tmp and /var/lib/redwood, several runtime pods terminated automatically. Pagerduty: PAGER-2318.
Sam (oncall): I’m on it. paging @Nora and @Jamal. any customer-facing impact yet?
Nora (SRE): ACK. I'm seeing a spike in OOM/killed messages tied to container log growth and a tmpfs mount filling up. Affected node group: g6-infer-*-usw2.
Jamal (EngRuntime): Confirmed — runtime crashed with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` repeated after restart, but root cause looks like rapid pod terminations due to disk/full writes. Model cache path is on ephemeral `/var/lib/redwood/model-cache` which is at 98%.
Priya (Infra): On-call node metrics: inode utilization also high — likely many small files (logs/journald).
Elena (Support): Tickets opening: two customers reporting failed inferences and 5xxs: TKT-5421, TKT-5423. Notified account owners, they want ETA.
Sam (oncall): Immediate mitigations? Can we cordon/evacuate nodes or clear logs quickly?
Nora (SRE): Plan: 1) isolate a node to run cleanup script; 2) scale down non-critical workloads; 3) rotate logs and delete old model-cache temp shards.
Jamal (EngRuntime): Agreed. I can push a runtime patch to prevent aggressive checkpoint writes for 10m. Will prepare a hotfix flag to disable verbose debug logging.
Priya (Infra): Doing a rolling cordon of most-affected nodes now. Command: ```kubectl cordon g6-infer-12-usw2 && kubectl drain g6-infer-12-usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force``` 
Nora (SRE): I ran `ssh node-12` and checked disk: ```# df -h /var/lib/redwood
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/nvme0n1p1  200G  196G  2.0G  99% /var/lib/redwood
``` And `sudo du -sh /var/lib/redwood/*`: large dirs: `model-cache/tmp-logs  88G`, `journal  34G`.
Sam (oncall): Can someone run immediate cleanup command to rotate and purge logs? We need to free ~20-30GB to get nodes stable.
Nora (SRE): Running cleanup now: ```sudo systemctl stop docker && rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/model-cache/tmp-logs/* && journalctl --vacuum-size=500M && systemctl start docker``` Will preserve active cache files.
Kai (Platform): Heads-up: deleting files in model-cache could cause temporary cold starts. We should route traffic to dedicated capacity or fallback model smaller. Adding a temporary traffic policy: route non-SLA to small-ram model variants.
Jamal (EngRuntime): Pushing runtime flag `REDWOOD_CACHE_WRITE_MODE=deferred` to affected daemonset to reduce writes. ```kubectl set env ds/serve-runtime REDWOOD_CACHE_WRITE_MODE=deferred -n redwood-prod``` 
Elena (Support): Noted re: customer impact. TKT-5421 says 40% error rate for a specific workspace — letting them know we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA.
Sam (oncall): Who's tracking a workaround for survivors? Need to prevent auto-scaling from moving more pods onto these nodes.
Priya (Infra): Putting a taint on nodes until we complete remediation: ```kubectl taint nodes node-12 redwood/disk-pressure=true:NoSchedule``` 
Nora (SRE): After cleanup freed ~45GB, node disk at 78%. Started re-scheduling some pods slowly. Watching for crash loops.
Jamal (EngRuntime): I see a few runtimes still crash-looping due to corrupted tmp shard references. I’m evicting and restarting pods after clearing tmp shards per-pod: ```kubectl delete pod <pod> -n redwood-prod``` 
Sam (oncall): Update on PD: PAGER-2318 acknowledged. ETA for stabilization?
Nora (SRE): Node stable for 6m, error rate dropped from 18% -> 2% on affected routes. Keeping cordon on two nodes until autoscaler flows down.
Kai (Platform): Added temporary autoscaler constraint to avoid scaling into g6-infer-12-* group. Also added logrotate config to runtime DaemonSet as emergency: rotate daily, max 200M.
Elena (Support): Customers notified: initial mitigation done, offered extended logs and follow-up. Two customers requested compensation; directed to CS ops.
Jamal (EngRuntime): Hotfix deployed: debug logs off, deferred cache writes flag set. Monitor for CUDA errors after restarts.
Nora (SRE): Observed one `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` right after restart — looks transient; no recurring pattern after caches cleared.
Sam (oncall): Good. Postmortem owners? Nora + Jamal for RCA, Priya for infra changes, Kai for platform follow-ups. Timeline: incident declared 1898765432, mitigated 1898766300, handoff at 1898766410.
Priya (Infra): Action items (short): - Ensure journal vacuum policy cluster-wide - Move model-cache to larger ephemeral partition or bind-mount to local SSD - Add liveness probe to prevent noisy restarts from filling logs - Add alert for inode usage (not just byte usage)
Jamal (EngRuntime): Action items (runtime): - Add write-back throttling and safer rollback for cache writes - Add graceful shutdown hooks to flush/rename temp files - Add telemetry to catch rapid small-file churn
Nora (SRE): I’ll draft preliminary postmortem and schedule a blameless review. Will include timeline and customer impact.
Sam (oncall): Passing to follow-up owners. Thanks all for fast responses. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — PAGER-2318 marked mitigated at 1898766300. Postmortem assigned to Nora.
Elena (Support): Closing the loop with customers now, will attach logs after postmortem.
